sn55.3:1.2: This is Dīghāvu’s only appearance in the Suttas. A fabled wise prince of the same name features in a long Vinaya story ([pli-tv-kd10:2.3.1]()).
sn55.3:4.5: text doesn’t identify the speaker, and BB has no note. But the use of tata, and the way of referring to the Buddha in the next sentence, show that it must be Jotika who is speaking here. But since this may not be clear in translation, I add it explicitly.
